instructions: Goal: find_coaching_brain; 1:1: find_personal_coach. Program: search_phorme_programs. Sport: preview_sport_week. Race: find_races, plan_for_race. Workout: preview_workout_import, find_exercise_swap. Places: find_gym_class, book_gym_class, find_clinic. Gym owner: check_place_in_ai, get_gym_report. Log: get_training_history, get_lift_progress, get_planned_sessions. Show warnings; confirm writes; share links, then render_training_import. Use only tool output; invent no ids, dates, loads. No prices.

tools.name: preview_workout_import
tools.title: Preview workout in Phorme
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a single workout they can follow and track in Phorme: one written in this conversation, pasted from notes, or built to fit their time and equipment. It checks the workout, matches each exercise to the Phorme movement library with a demo link, flags anything that needs equipment the user did not list or runs past their time, and stores a private preview for 24 hours. It does not save training to any account. Do not use it for multiweek programs, nutrition plans, or pain and injury questions.

workout.description: The workout to preview, taken from this conversation.

title.description: Workout name, for example "Lower body strength".

notes.description: Short note for the whole workout.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: Expected length of the workout in minutes.

exercises.description: Exercises in the order they are performed. At most 300 sets in total.

name.description: Exercise name as written in the conversation, for example "Back squat".

reps.description: Reps per set as short text, for example "8", "8-10", "AMRAP" or "40 sec".

rest.description: Rest between sets, for example "90 sec" or "2 min".

duration.description: Work time in seconds for a timed exercise.

load.description: Target load, for example "80%", "135 lb", "60 kg", "bodyweight" or "RPE 8".

notes.description: Short coaching note for this exercise.

available_equipment.description: Equipment the user said they have, for example ["dumbbells", "bench"] or ["none"]. Leave out when the user did not say.

time_limit_minutes.description: Minutes the user said they have. Leave out when the user did not say.

origin.description: Use "sport_week" when the workout is a session returned by preview_sport_week. Otherwise leave out.

preview_id.description: Identifies this preview when it is saved.

expires_at.description: When the preview can no longer be saved, as an ISO 8601 time.

warnings.description: Items the user should review before saving.

requires_confirmation.description: Always true: saving needs the user's confirmation.

exercises.description: Each exercise with its Phorme library match and demo link.

library_name.description: The Phorme movement it matched, or null when nothing matched.

equipment_ok.description: Whether that fits the equipment the user listed. Null when no equipment was given or the library does not say.

tools.name: save_workout_to_phorme
tools.title: Save workout to Phorme
tools.description: Use this when the user has seen a workout preview and clearly said to save it. It saves that preview to the connected Phorme account as a private workout and returns a link that opens it in Phorme. It needs a connected Phorme account with the training:write permission. Retrying with the same idempotency_key returns the same saved workout and does not create a second copy.

preview_id.description: The preview_id of the preview being saved.

confirmation.description: Set to true only after the user clearly confirmed this save in the conversation.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string for this save. Reuse the same value when retrying so no second copy is created.

open_url.description: Link that opens the saved training in Phorme.

tools.name: preview_program_import
tools.title: Preview program in Phorme
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to turn a multiweek training program from this conversation into trackable Phorme training. It checks every week and workout, matches exercises to the Phorme movement library, and stores a private preview for 24 hours. It does not save training to any account. Do not use it for a single workout, nutrition plans or medical questions.

program.description: The multiweek program to preview, taken from this conversation. At most 500 workouts in total.

title.description: Program name, for example "Four week strength base".

difficulty.description: Intended training level. Defaults to intermediate.

week_number.description: Week position in the program, starting at 1. Each week_number appears once.

focus.description: Short focus for the week, for example "Volume".

day_number.description: Day position within the week, starting at 1. Each day_number appears once in a week.

title.description: Workout name, for example "Lower body strength".

notes.description: Short note for the whole workout.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: Expected length of the workout in minutes.

exercises.description: Exercises in the order they are performed. At most 300 sets in total.

name.description: Exercise name as written in the conversation, for example "Back squat".

reps.description: Reps per set as short text, for example "8", "8-10", "AMRAP" or "40 sec".

rest.description: Rest between sets, for example "90 sec" or "2 min".

duration.description: Work time in seconds for a timed exercise.

load.description: Target load, for example "80%", "135 lb", "60 kg", "bodyweight" or "RPE 8".

notes.description: Short coaching note for this exercise.

preview_id.description: Identifies this preview when it is saved.

expires_at.description: When the preview can no longer be saved, as an ISO 8601 time.

warnings.description: Items the user should review before saving.

requires_confirmation.description: Always true: saving needs the user's confirmation.

exercises.description: Each exercise with its Phorme library match and demo link.

library_name.description: The Phorme movement it matched, or null when nothing matched.

equipment_ok.description: Whether that fits the equipment the user listed. Null when no equipment was given or the library does not say.

tools.name: save_program_to_phorme
tools.title: Save program to Phorme
tools.description: Use this when the user has seen a program preview and clearly said to save it. It saves that preview to the connected Phorme account as a private program and returns a link that opens it in Phorme. It needs a connected Phorme account with the training:write permission and a Phorme membership that already includes programs. If the account does not have that membership the tool says so and saves nothing. It never starts a purchase. Retrying with the same idempotency_key does not create a second copy.

preview_id.description: The preview_id of the preview being saved.

confirmation.description: Set to true only after the user clearly confirmed this save in the conversation.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string for this save. Reuse the same value when retrying so no second copy is created.

open_url.description: Link that opens the saved training in Phorme.

tools.name: get_saved_training
tools.title: Get saved Phorme training
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about a workout or program already saved to Phorme in this conversation, for example to get its Phorme link again. It returns the title and open link for training owned by the connected Phorme account and changes nothing. It needs the training_id from that save. It cannot list, search, edit or delete training.

training_kind.description: Whether the saved item is a workout or a program.

training_id.description: The training_id returned by save_workout_to_phorme or save_program_to_phorme.

open_url.description: Link that opens the saved training in Phorme.

tools.name: render_training_import
tools.title: Show Phorme training card
tools.description: Use this to show a compact Phorme card for a workout or program that was just previewed or saved. It displays only the title, counts, status and link it is given. It reads and changes nothing in Phorme.

title.description: Training title from the tool result.

status.description: "preview" for training not yet saved, "saved" for training saved to Phorme.

open_url.description: Link that opens the saved training in Phorme. Not set for previews.

title.description: Training title from the tool result.

status.description: "preview" for training not yet saved, "saved" for training saved to Phorme.

open_url.description: Link that opens the saved training in Phorme. Not set for previews.

tools.name: preview_sport_week
tools.title: Plan a sport training week
tools.description: Use this when the user plays a sport and wants their gym days for a week planned around it, for example two lifting days during basketball season. It picks the closest coach-built Phorme sport program and returns one week of sessions sized to the days the user has, with sets, reps, coach notes and a demo link for each exercise. It reads only and changes nothing in any account. If Phorme has no program for that sport it says so in match_quality and limits. Do not use it for injury rehab, team practice plans for children, or nutrition.

sport.description: The sport or position, for example "basketball", "volleyball" or "wide receiver".

gym_days_per_week.description: Gym days the user has this week. Ask when the user did not say.

season_phase.description: Where the user is in their season, only if they said.

match_quality.description: exact_sport: a program written for this sport. related: the closest program. none: a general athletic program.

brain.description: The coaching brain whose method the week follows: name, coach, focus, how_it_trains and image_url (Phorme's own picture). Name it to the user.

program.description: The coach-built program the week comes from.

sessions.description: One entry per gym day, each with a title and exercises.

limits.description: What this week does not cover. Tell the user.

tools.name: find_races
tools.title: Find a race
tools.description: Use this when the user is looking for a race to enter, for example "which 70.3 can I do in South America next spring", "marathons in Europe in April" or "a HYROX near Riga". It lists races from Phorme's verified race listings that fit the kind of race, the place (a country, city or region) and the months asked, by date only, each with its city, date, its own page, its registration as the organiser last showed it, and whether Phorme has a plan that counts back to it. When the organiser has given them, the race's own logistics are included: where to pick up the race packet, the nearest airport, getting there and the official hotels the organiser lists, with the page they came from. It reads only and changes nothing. Only races in Phorme's listings are returned, with the dates the listings give.

kind.description: The kind of race, for example "70.3", "triathlon", "marathon", "half marathon" or "HYROX". Leave out for any.

where.description: A country, city or region, for example "Colombia", "Barranquilla" or "South America". Leave out for anywhere.

from_month.description: First month, YYYY-MM, only if the user gave a window.

to_month.description: Last month, YYYY-MM, only if the user gave a window.

races.description: Races by date: name, city, country, on (YYYY-MM-DD or null), url (the race's own page), registration (status open, sold_out, opening_soon or closed, its url and checked_on, or null), has_plan, and logistics (the race's own venue, packet pickup, airport, official hotels and guide links as the organiser listed them, with source_url and checked_on; null when not given).

limits.description: Where the dates come from and what to check. Tell the user.

tools.name: plan_for_race
tools.title: Plan training for a race
tools.description: Use this when the user names a race they are training for, for example "IRONMAN 70.3 Barranquilla", "I signed up for the half ironman in Cartagena" or "Chicago Marathon". It finds the race in Phorme's race listings (name, date, city and the race's own page), counts the weeks to race day, and returns the week of Phorme's plan for that kind of race that lines up with race day, with sets, reps, paces, coach notes and a demo link for each exercise. For a triathlon (IRONMAN 70.3, 5150, full) it is swim, bike and run in one plan, with efforts until the athlete's swim and bike tests are in. When the organiser has given them, the race's own logistics come with it (venue, where to pick up the race packet, airport, official hotels from the organiser), with the page and date they were read. It reads only and changes nothing. If the race is not listed it says so; never guess a race date. Do not use it for injury rehab or nutrition.

race.description: The race as the user named it, for example "IRONMAN 70.3 Barranquilla".

The race as listed: name, city, country, on (YYYY-MM-DD, null when not yet published), url (the race's own page), registration, and logistics: the race's own venue, packet_pickup, airport, getting_there, hotels (up to 6 official hotels, each name, url and note), course_url, athlete_guide_url, source_url and checked_on, as the organiser listed them, or null.

starts_on.description: When the race is further off than the plan, the day the plan's first week starts.

brain.description: The Phorme coaching brain the plan follows: name, coach and how_it_trains.

program.description: The plan: title, weeks and days_per_week, and its summary.

week_number.description: The week of the plan these sessions are.

sessions.description: The sessions of that week, each with a title and exercises.

limits.description: What this plan does not cover and where its dates come from. Tell the user.

tools.name: find_coaching_brain
tools.title: Find a Phorme coaching brain
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a way to train for a goal or sport, for example "I want to get more explosive for basketball", "build muscle three days a week" or "train for a half marathon", or wants to train with a named coach, for example "train with Cameron Goodson", and has not picked a programme. Phorme coaching brains are curated training methods: a coach, the principles the method trains by, and a coach-built programme. It returns up to three brains that fit, best first, each with its coach, focus, how it trains and its programmes with weeks and days a week; with a coach named, only that coach's brains. It reads only and changes nothing. Do not use it for injury rehab or nutrition.

goal.description: What the user wants from training, in their words, for example "jump higher" or "first HYROX race".

sport.description: The sport or position, only if the user named one.

days_per_week.description: Training days a week, only if the user said.

coach.description: A coach the user named, for example "Cameron Goodson". Only that coach's brains are returned.

brains.description: Best fit first: id, name, coach, coach_title, focus, how_it_trains, image_url and image_alt (Phorme's own picture of the brain, its programme cover or its coach's room: show it, never a web photo), programmes (name, summary, weeks, days_per_week, image_url) and why it fits.

limits.description: What this does not cover. Tell the user.

tools.name: find_gym_class
tools.title: Find a Phorme gym or class
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a gym, studio or class to train at in person, for example "a strength class in Austin this week" or "a gym near me". It returns up to five Phorme gyms, studios and other places to train in the city named or within 60 km (or radius_km) of the position given, nearest or best matching first, each with its page on phor.me and its classes in the coming days with the class id, local start time, length, places left and a link to book on phor.me. When nothing matches it returns alternatives: the nearest places further out, and a home plan from a Phorme coaching brain. It reads only and shows no prices; booking a class for a signed-in user is a separate step.

annotations.title: Find a Phorme gym or class

city.description: The city the user named, for example "Austin".

near_lat.description: Latitude, only if the user shared their position.

near_lon.description: Longitude, only if the user shared their position.

class_type.description: The kind of class, only if the user said, for example "barbell" or "yoga".

days.description: How many days ahead to look. Default 7.

radius_km.description: How far from the shared position to look, in km. Default 60. Use a larger one only when the user said they would travel.

places.description: Gyms, studios and other places to train, nearest or best matching first: place_id, name, kind, line, city, country, distance_km, page_url and classes (class_id, the id book_gym_class takes, then title, line, starts, minutes, spots_left, book_url).

limits.description: What this does not cover. Tell the user.

alternatives.description: When nothing matched or no class is scheduled: kind (wider_radius, other_cities, home_plan), line (what to offer), tool, and for wider_radius the nearest places further out. Offer them; never leave the user with nothing.

tools.name: book_gym_class
tools.title: Book a Phorme gym class
tools.description: Use this when a signed-in user wants a place in one class at a Phorme gym or studio. Confirm the class, the day and time, and the gym with the user first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. It books the class for the connected Phorme account: booked when there is a spot, on the waitlist when it is full, a spot held for 15 minutes when the class is paid, or a request the gym is told about when the gym has not opened booking on Phorme yet. A paid class is paid on Phorme's own payment page, through a link in the result. This tool takes no payment, names no amount and never sells a subscription or membership. Booking the same class again returns the same booking. It needs a connected Phorme account with the training:write permission.

class_id.description: The class_id of the class, from find_gym_class.

place_id.description: The place_id of its gym or studio, from the same find_gym_class result.

confirmation.description: Set to true only after the user said yes to this class, day, time and gym.

status.description: booked: the user is in. waitlisted: the class is full; Phorme moves them up if a spot opens. pending_payment: the spot is held 15 minutes while they pay at pay_url. requested: the gym is told they asked; held up to 7 days, not a booking yet. book_on_phorme: nothing was booked; give them book_url.

class.description: title, starts (local time at the gym) and minutes.

place.description: name, city and page_url of the gym or studio.

pay_url.description: Phorme's own payment page for this booking, only when status is pending_payment.

next.description: What to tell the user next.

tools.name: cancel_gym_booking
tools.title: Cancel a Phorme gym booking
tools.description: Use this when a signed-in user wants to give up a class they booked, are on the waitlist for, or asked a gym for on Phorme. Confirm which class with the user first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. It cancels that booking for the connected Phorme account and frees the spot for the next person on the waitlist. It takes the booking id, or the class id of the booked class. Sales are final, so a paid class is not refunded. It needs a connected Phorme account with the training:write permission.

booking_id.description: The booking_id from book_gym_class. Give this or class_id.

class_id.description: The class_id of the booked class, when the booking_id is not known.

confirmation.description: Set to true only after the user said yes to cancelling this class.

next.description: What to tell the user next.

tools.name: find_clinic
tools.title: Find a Phorme clinic
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to be seen in person by a physical therapist, sports medicine clinic, chiropractor, sports massage therapist or recovery studio, in a city they name or near a position they share. It returns up to five Phorme clinic and recovery partners, nearest or best matching first, each with the kind of care, the services it lists, its page on phor.me and a link to ask for an appointment there. It takes a place and a kind of care, never symptoms. It reads only, does not diagnose or treat, shows no prices and books nothing.

city.description: The city the user named, for example "Austin".

near_lat.description: Latitude, only if the user shared their position.

near_lon.description: Longitude, only if the user shared their position.

care.description: The kind of care the user asked for, only if they named one.

clinics.description: Clinics, nearest or best matching first: name, care, line, city, country, distance_km, page_url, request_url and services.

limits.description: What this does not cover. Tell the user.

tools.name: find_personal_coach
tools.title: Find a personal coach
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a human coach of their own: 1:1 coaching, someone who writes their program for them, checks in each week, reviews how they move or answers their messages, for example "I want a real coach for basketball" or "can someone coach me one on one?". It returns the Phorme coaches taking 1:1 clients now, with what the coaching includes, how many spots are open and the coach's page, where the terms and joining are. It shows no prices, books nothing and changes nothing. Coaching is training, not medical care.

goal.description: What the user wants coaching for, in their words, only if they said.

sport.description: Their sport, only if they named one.

coaches.description: Each coach taking 1:1 clients: coach, coach_url, offer, summary, includes, spots (status, detail, open), page_url, how_it_starts, and free_review (open, page_url) when the coach has a free plan review spot this week.

limits.description: What this does not cover. Tell the user.

tools.name: check_place_in_ai
tools.title: Check a gym, clinic or race in AI answers
tools.description: Use this when the owner or manager of a gym, studio, sports clinic or race asks whether ChatGPT knows their place or race or recommends it, for example "does ChatGPT recommend my gym?", "what does AI say about my physio clinic in Austin?" or "does ChatGPT know our triathlon?". It asks OpenAI's model with web search two questions a customer or athlete would ask: about the place or race, and for the best of its kind in its city. It returns whether it was found, whether it was named among the best and who was named instead, which of five facts a customer needs were stated (where, hours, classes or treatments, prices, how to book; for a race: where it starts, race date, course, entry fee, how to register), the pages it cited, and a link to the full result. Prices are reported only as stated or not, and a fact counts as stated only when the answer gave it. It also returns a free next step: a link to claim the place on Phorme (for a race, the race organiser page). It takes up to a minute, reuses a check of the same place from the last week, and saves the result as a share page; it changes nothing about the place on Phorme. It is for owners and managers, not for rating a place for someone choosing where to go.

annotations.title: Check a gym, clinic or race in AI answers

place.description: The gym, clinic or race's name, as the owner or organiser wrote it.

city.description: The city it is in (for a race, where it is held).

kind.description: What kind of place it is, as a customer would search. Defaults to gyms.

identified.description: Whether ChatGPT found this specific place.

named_in_best_of_city.description: Whether it was named when asked for the best of its kind in the city.

named_instead.description: Places named instead, when it was not.

facts.description: Each fact a customer needs: fact, stated, value (null for prices).

result_url.description: The full result on gyms.phor.me. Share it.

next_step_url.description: Free next step: claim the place on Phorme (a race: the organiser page). It names no price.

next_step.description: What the next step does, in one line.

limits.description: What this check does not show. Tell the user.

tools.name: find_exercise_swap
tools.title: Find an exercise swap
tools.description: Use this when the user needs a replacement for one exercise because they do not have the equipment, the station is taken, or they want a different option, for example no cable machine for cable rows. It returns up to five Phorme library movements of the same kind that the user's equipment allows, each with a demo link, and says so when it has to offer the nearest kind instead. It reads only and changes nothing, including any saved plan. Do not use it to work around pain or injury.

exercise.description: The exercise to replace, as the user wrote it, for example "Seated cable row".

available_equipment.description: Equipment the user has, for example ["dumbbells", "bench"] or ["none"]. Ask when the user did not say.

reason.description: Why they need a swap, only if they said.

matched.description: The Phorme library movement the exercise matched.

pattern.description: The kind of movement, for example horizontal_pull.

match.description: nearest_kind: nothing of the same kind fits the equipment, so these work the same muscles from a different angle.

swaps.description: Replacements, best first, each with name, equipment and demo_url.

limits.description: What the swaps do not cover. Tell the user.

tools.name: get_training_history
tools.title: Get my Phorme training log
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about their own training logged in Phorme: what they did last time, how often they trained, their personal records, or a next workout built on their recent sessions. It returns their most recent logged workouts with each exercise's sets, best set, estimated max and volume, how many workouts they logged in the last 7 and 30 days, and their latest records. It reads only and changes nothing. It needs a connected Phorme account. Weights are in pounds.

limit.description: How many recent workouts to return, newest first. Defaults to 10.

found.description: False when this account has no Phorme training yet.

workouts.description: Newest first: date, title, minutes and exercises with sets, best_set, e1rm_lb and volume_lb.

records.description: Latest personal records: movement, label, value and date.

tools.name: get_lift_progress
tools.title: Chart my lift progress
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how one of their lifts is progressing or wants it graphed, for example "how is my bench going" or "chart my squat over six months". It finds the lift in their Phorme log by the words they use and returns one point per session with the best set, estimated max and volume, the change over the period and their best session, and shows a chart card. It reads only and changes nothing. It needs a connected Phorme account. Weights are in pounds. If no lift matched it lists the lifts they have logged.

movement.description: The lift as the user said it, for example "bench", "back squat" or "RDL".

months.description: How many months back to look. Defaults to 6.

movement.description: The logged lift that matched, or null.

also_matched.description: Other logged lifts the words also matched.

points.description: Oldest first: on, top_set, e1rm_lb, volume_lb, sets.

change.description: from_e1rm_lb, to_e1rm_lb, change_lb and change_pct over the period.

logged_movements.description: When nothing matched: the lifts they log most.

tools.name: get_planned_sessions
tools.title: Get my planned Phorme sessions
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what their Phorme plan has for today or the coming days, for example "what is my workout today". It returns each planned session with its exercises, sets, reps and the loads Phorme set from their own maxes. It reads only and changes nothing, including the plan. It needs a connected Phorme account. Weights are in pounds.

days.description: How many days ahead, starting today. Defaults to 7.

plan.description: The name of the plan they follow.

sessions.description: In date order: on, title, status, minutes and exercises with sets, target, load and note.

tools.name: get_my_coaching_business
tools.title: Get my coaching brains
tools.description: Use this when a Phorme coach asks about their own coaching brains: how many members train under each, who went quiet, what they have earned, and whether a note to members can go today. It reads only and changes nothing. It needs a connected Phorme account; an account without a coaching brain gets the address of the coach console.

coach.description: Whether the account has an active coach plan.

brains.description: Each brain with status, member totals, quiet members (labels only), earnings in cents and whether a note may go today.

tools.name: start_my_coaching_brain
tools.title: Start my coaching brain
tools.description: Use this when a coach or trainer wants to turn their own method into a Phorme coaching brain and has none yet, or asks for a new one. It creates a draft brain with the name they chose and their method in their own words; members see nothing until the coach publishes it in the coach console. A first program can then be saved to it as a draft. It needs a connected Phorme account; signing in with a phone number creates one.

name.description: The brain's name, as the coach chose it, for example "Hayes Strength".

tagline.description: One line on who it is for, in the coach's words.

method.description: How the coach trains people, in their own words from this conversation. Never invented.

confirmation.description: True only after the coach confirmed the name and method.

tools.name: save_program_to_my_coaching_brain
tools.title: Save a program to my coaching brain
tools.description: Use this when a Phorme coach has written a program in this conversation and clearly said to save it to one of their coaching brains. It saves the program as a draft on that brain (session names, exercises, sets and reps); members see nothing until the coach adds the draft in the coach console. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the brain.

annotations.title: Save a program to my coaching brain

brain_id.description: The brain id from the coach's brains.

weeks.description: How many weeks the program runs. Defaults to 4.

sessions.description: One week of sessions; the app repeats and progresses it.

reps.description: Reps per set, for example 8 or "8-10".

seconds.description: For timed sets instead of reps.

confirmation.description: True only after the coach confirmed this save.

tools.name: send_note_to_my_members
tools.title: Send a note to my members
tools.description: Use this when a Phorme coach has written a short note to everyone training under one of their published coaching brains and clearly said to send it. It sends the coach's words as they are, as a notification and in each member's coach history: up to 400 characters, no links, one note per brain per day. It needs a connected Phorme account with an active coach plan that owns the brain.

tools.name: get_gym_report
tools.title: Get my gym report
tools.description: Use this when a gym, studio or clinic owner asks about their own places on Phorme: what is listed, what is live, and how each place did, for example "how is my gym doing on Phorme?" or "did anyone book this week?". It returns each place the connected account lists, with its page and status, and its report: times shown by assistants, page views, asks held, bookings, requests, members and the share earned. A place on the free listing shows a little reach and what it missed; the rest is locked, the same as the web console. It reads only and changes nothing. It needs a connected Phorme account.

tools.name: create_or_claim_place
tools.title: List or claim my place
tools.description: Use this when a gym, studio or clinic owner wants their place on Phorme, for example after an AI check, or says "list my gym". Confirm the name, city and address with the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. It lists the place for the connected account as a draft nobody sees yet, with its page facts, and finds the map pin from the address. If the account already lists a place with that name in that city it returns that place and changes nothing. Listing is free; it takes no payment and starts no plan. It needs a connected Phorme account.

tools.name: set_class_schedule
tools.title: Set my class schedule
tools.description: Use this when an owner wants to see, add, change or cancel a class at their place. action list reads the schedule and changes nothing. For add, edit and cancel, read the class, day and time back to the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. A class people booked keeps its time, length and price; a class members paid for cannot be cancelled here. Members pay for a paid class on Phorme's own payment page; this tool takes no payment. tools.name: publish_place
tools.title: Put my place live
tools.description: Use this when an owner wants their place live on Phorme: its page on phor.me, the app's map and the Phorme connector. Confirm with the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. Going live needs an email for booking confirmations and requests: request_email, else the place's own, else the account's. Listing is free; when someone asks to book a place that is not on the gym plan, the ask is held 7 days and the owner is told. It takes no payment and starts no plan. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: start_gym_brain
tools.title: Start my gym's coaching brain
tools.description: Use this when an owner wants a coaching brain for their place, so members train with the gym's own coach in the Phorme app. Confirm with the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. In one step it makes a brain from the place's name, line and classes, gives it a starting program from the Phorme library, publishes it and puts the place's members under it, the same as the console's one-click start. The owner can change it in the builder after. Free on the free listing too. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: set_member_cover
tools.title: Cover my members
tools.description: Use this when an owner on the gym plan wants to pay for their members' Phorme membership at one place, so members train free, or wants to stop. Confirm with the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. It turns the switch on or off and can lower the cap of members covered (up to 50). Members join from the app and the place approves them. A place not on the gym plan cannot turn it on; the result then gives plan_url, the plan on phor.me. It takes no payment here. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: list_held_requests
tools.title: List asks waiting for my gym
tools.description: Use this when an owner asks who wants to book or visit their place, for example "who asked to book this week?". At a place not on the gym plan, class bookings and 1:1 requests are held for 7 days. It returns each one waiting: its hold_id, the place, the class and its local time (or that it is a 1:1 request), the member's first name, their note and best times, when it expires, and whether it can be accepted now. It reads only and changes nothing. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: answer_held_request
tools.title: Answer an ask waiting for my gym
tools.description: Use this when an owner wants to accept or decline one ask held for the plan at their place, by its hold_id. Read the ask back to the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. Accept books the member in (a paid class is held while they pay on Phorme's own page; a full class puts them on the waitlist), or sends a 1:1 request on to the place's email. Decline ends it, with the owner's short note when they gave one. Either way the member hears. Accepting needs the gym plan at that place; the result then gives plan_url instead. It takes no payment. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: claim_place
tools.title: Claim a place nobody runs
tools.description: Use this when an owner says a gym Phorme already lists is theirs and nobody runs it on Phorme yet, for example "that gym is mine". Confirm the place with the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. It never hands the place over by itself: Phorme sends a six digit code to the email or phone the place has on file, not to the person asking. Whoever reads that inbox or phone gives them the code, and entering it makes them the owner. A place with neither on file waits for Phorme's team. It takes no payment. It needs a connected Phorme account.

tools.name: verify_place_claim
tools.title: Enter my place claim code
tools.description: Use this when an owner has the six digit code Phorme sent to their place's own email or phone after they claimed it. Read the code back to the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. A right code makes the connected account the place's owner; a wrong one changes nothing, and after five wrong tries or 24 hours the place must be claimed again. It takes no payment. It needs a connected Phorme account.

tools.name: cover_member
tools.title: Cover one member
tools.description: Use this when an owner on the gym plan wants to see who is covered or asked to be at one place, or to invite, approve or remove one member, for example "invite my member Sam to train free". action list reads who is listed and changes nothing. For invite (by the member's phone), approve (a member who asked) and remove, read it back to the owner first, and set confirmation to true only after they said yes. An invite sends the phone a text to join; the member hears once when they are covered or removed. Cover counts only while the gym plan covers the place, up to its cap; past it, new members pay as normal. It takes no payment here. It needs a connected Phorme account that owns the place.

tools.name: search_phorme_programs
tools.title: Search Phorme programs
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for an existing coach-built training program for their sport or goal, for example a structured volleyball program. It returns up to five matching Phorme programs, each with a sample session from its first week that the user can try now and where to find it in the Phorme app. Every result is a program a member can train in the Phorme app today.
